general_notes: Each state has the same five kinds of candidate: (1) the sharp full painting scaled down inside a thin flat dark border, closest to the target; (2) soft square vignettes (two per state, which look the same as each other); (3) soft round vignettes (two or three per state; one per state in idle, joyful and depleted has a visibly tighter rim); (4) a heavily blurred full-frame copy; (5) a 3D/CG re-creation that is clearly a different rendering of the character. I saw no candidate that is pixel-identical to the target; the bordered versions come closest. In the in-app vignette versions the character itself is unchanged, so their character scores are held at 8.5-9 only because cropping and darkening touch the outer flames and the scale is reduced; their main losses are under P2-P4. In the depleted target there is an odd flat grey rectangle at the lower right; the vignette versions hide it. I scored that as a framing and integration difference, not a defect, which is debatable. Uncertainty: I judged at the displayed resolution, so small differences in sharpness between the vignette versions and the target (P1 8.5) are estimates; same-looking pairs were not checked pixel by pixel.
